title: Attestation Storyboard: SOC 2 + ISO Walkthroughs and Evidence Scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working 'storyboard' for auditor walkthroughs: concrete evidence scenarios we can demonstrate live (or hand over artifacts for remote review) that link RBAC v2 events, audit-log schema exports, SIEM ingestion, and evidence automation paths to specific SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls. The goal is to reduce last-minute discovery during audits by standardizing a set of representative scenarios and prepared Q&A for auditors.

Audience:
- Internal: security & compliance, infra, SRE, product security, solutions engineering.
- External: SOC 2 / ISO auditors (as pre-read or demo script).

Executive summary:
- We will present 5 evidence scenarios covering key control families: access management, change control, logging & monitoring, incident response, and data handling. Each scenario maps to the control language for SOC 2 CC6/CC7 and ISO A.9/A.12/A.16 respectively.
- For each scenario we list: trigger (what an engineer does), RBAC v2 events emitted, audit-log fields expected (per the current schema), SIEM pipeline transforms, automated evidence artifacts (signed export, CSV snapshot, Kibana query link), and likely auditor questions with suggested references.
- Where we have gaps (automation missing, event enrichments not present, retention gaps), they are called out with owner and remediation priority.

Scenario 1: Admin role change (access provisioning/deprovisioning)
- Trigger: engineering manager updates a user role from "developer" to "team-admin" in the Console (RBAC v2 UI).
- RBAC v2 events to capture: user.role.update, user.role.assign, user.role.remove (delta events).
- Audit-log schema (fields we will include): timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_email, actor_ip, target_user_id, target_user_email, org_id, workspace_id, old_roles, new_roles, reason (free text), request_id, trace_id, signed_by (service account).
- SIEM export considerations: event normalization: map actor_email -> principal.email, include identity.enrichment (SCIM id if available), tag event.source=console, route to access-management index.
- Evidence artifact: 1) signed JSONL export for the time window, 2) CSV snapshot with filtered columns (actor, target, diff, timestamp), 3) short demo video (1-2m) showing the Console change and corresponding log emission (for remote auditors).
- Anticipated auditor Qs & prepared answers: Q: How do you verify who initiated the change? A: audit-log signed_by + principal authentication logs + session token trace id; cross-check SSO IdP assertion (linked artifact: SSO assertion export).
- Gap: we currently do not persist 'reason' for change in structured field (freeform only). Remediation: add UI required field or dropdown for change reason (owner: Jun Park, priority: P2).

Scenario 2: Service account key rotation (secrets/change control)
- Trigger: Platform rotates a service account key via the key-management job.
- RBAC v2 events: service_account.key.rotate, service_account.key.create, service_account.key.revoke.
- Audit-log fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id (system-job), actor_service, target_service_account_id, key_id, rotation_window, rotation_policy_id, request_id, change_metadata (previous_key_id masked), approval_ticket_id (if manual step).
- SIEM mapping: mark as high-risk change; route to infra-changes index and generate an alert if rotation happens outside scheduled window.
- Evidence artifact: rotation runbook (versioned), signed change event, rotation job run logs, Jira ticket link for manual approvals.
- Gap: automated linkage between rotation event and Jira approval ticket for semi-manual rotations. Remediation: enrich rotation job to attach approval_ticket_id automatically (owner: Aidan Murphy).

Scenario 3: High-latency or error spike detection (monitoring & incident)
- Trigger: Serving runtime emits error rate spike and latency > SLA on a model route.
- Events: metric.alert.create, route.latency.spike, route.error.rate.threshold.
- Audit-log fields: timestamp, alert_id, route_id, model_version, pod_ids, sample_request_ids, downstream_impacted_services, initiated_by (auto/engineer), severity.
- SIEM pipeline: ingest metrics alerts as structured incidents, correlate with recent deploy events (deploy.job.*), enrich with rollout state and canary percentage.
- Evidence artifact: incident ticket, timeline exported (CSV), post-incident analysis doc, continuous-monitoring dashboard snapshot (PNG) with UTC timestamp overlay.
- Auditor Qs: show how we detect and triage anomalies and what rollback authority exists. Prepared demo: query in SIEM for alert_id -> join deploy events -> show canary percentage and rollback action.
- Gap: sample_request_ids currently truncated for long-running requests. Remediation: increase sample window retention to 48h for flagged routes (owner: Rosa Alvarez, priority: P1).

Scenario 4: Cross-account data access attempt (data handling & least privilege)
- Trigger: attempt to retrieve embeddings for dataset belonging to another org via API key misuse.
- RBAC v2 events: api_key.access_attempt, data.access.denied, policy.eval.result.
- Audit-log fields: timestamp, event_id, api_key_id (hashed), requester_principal, resource_id, resource_owner_org, action, decision (allow/deny), policy_version, reason_code, location_ip, geo.
- SIEM behavior: generate an AV/Alert for denied cross-org access with severity elevated if same API key appears in >3 org scopes in 24h.
- Evidence artifact: deny trail export, blocked-request sample (headers masked), policy evaluation snapshot, revocation action (if any).
- Auditor Qs: how do you prove least privilege is enforced? Answer: show policy eval decision history + runtime enforcement points + tests in CI that exercise policy. Linked artifact: policy-e2e test run (github link).
- Gap: we lack a canned report that summarizes 'denied cross-org events last 90 days' for auditors. Remediation: add quarterly report generator (owner: Priya Natarajan).

Scenario 5: New model onboarding (change control + quality gates)
- Trigger: Research team publishes a new model to the model catalog and marks it available for production.
- RBAC v2 events: model.version.publish, model.version.approve, model.catalog.update.
- Audit-log fields: timestamp, model_id, version_id, publisher_id, approval_workflow_id, canary_route, rollout_percentage, eval_suite_id, evaluation_results_hash.
- SIEM pipeline: tag model change events, correlate with performance regression alerts and quality gates.
- Evidence artifact: model onboarding checklist, evaluation report, approval tickets, model rollout timeline.
- Auditor Qs: how do you prevent regressions into production? Prepared answer: multi-stage rollout with automated rollback, pre/post evals stored in artifact store with signed hashes.
- Gap: evaluation results are stored in research buckets with shorter retention than audit evidence policy. Remediation: copy approved evals to evidence bucket with 7-year retention (owner: Justin Hale, priority: P1).

Cross-cutting audit-log schema notes (current vs desired):
- Current lightweight schema covers: timestamp, event_type, actor, target, request_id, trace_id, metadata(json blob).
- Desired additions (to make auditor-ready): structured "actor_email", "actor_mfa", "old_value", "new_value", "approval_ticket_id", "signed_by", "signature_alg", and standardized "resource_type" taxonomy.
- Reason: auditors prefer discrete columns rather than opaque metadata blobs; structured fields reduce follow-up questions and speed evidence collection.

Evidence automation playbook (how we'll produce artifacts reliably):
1) Scenario-triggered export jobs: small Lambda/cron jobs that assemble the scenario-specific fields for a given time window and store a signed snapshot in the evidence bucket.
2) Retention & immutability: evidence bucket uses WORM-style retention policies and KMS-managed keys; snapshots are versioned.
3) Hash and sign: each snapshot has SHA256 + service principal signature; signatures recorded in manifest.csv.
4) SIEM saved queries: canonical saved searches per scenario with documented steps to reproduce; export links included in evidence bundle.
5) Demo artifacts: short recordings or step-by-step screenshots for UI-driven flows.

SIEM export checklist (operational requirements):
- Canonical field mappings (documented): event_type, timestamp, org_id, principal.email, principal.id, resource_type, resource_id, decision, reason_code, request_id, trace_id.
- Retention compliance: verify SIEM index retention matches control requirement (90 days for immediate logs, archives to cold for 7 years as evidence).
- Alert-to-ticket mapping: ensure every high-severity alert automatically creates a ticket with attached top-10 correlated events.
- Export signing: daily signed tarball of SIEM indices for audit window with manifest and digest.

Auditor Q&A (prepared short answers):
- Q: How do you prevent log tampering?
  A: Immutable evidence bucket with WORM retention + KMS-based signatures + SIEM write-only ingest with ACLs. Provide signed manifests.
- Q: How do you tie identity from SSO to audit events?
  A: We persist SSO assertion id as actor_id and principal.email and map session token trace_id across systems; we keep IdP logs for 90 days and can produce assertion export for an event_id.
- Q: What is your retention policy?
  A: Operational logs 90d hot, 365d warm, evidence exports archived for 7 years in compliance bucket with restricted access.
- Q: How do you show timely detection and response?
  A: Show SIEM alert timeline, ticket creation timestamp, incident timeline, and postmortem with remediation actions and SLAs.

Gap analysis summary (high level):
- Top priority (P1): missing structured fields for actor_email and approval_ticket_id in audit logs; retention mismatch for model evals.
- Medium (P2): missing required change reason field for RBAC updates; automation to link rotation jobs to approvals.
- Low (P3): additional canned reports for auditors (nice-to-have dashboards).

Action items & owners (short):
- Add actor_email and approval_ticket_id to audit schema (owner: Jun Park, due: 2025-03-12, status: in_progress).
- Build evidence export job for Scenario 1 and 4 (owner: Priya Natarajan, due: 2025-03-20).
- Copy approved model evals to evidence bucket with retention policy (owner: Justin Hale, due: 2025-03-01, status: blocked by infra quota).
- Implement rotation->ticket linkage (owner: Aidan Murphy, due: 2025-04-01).
- Create SIEM saved queries and demo scripts for auditors (owner: Rosa Alvarez, due: 2025-03-08).

Demo / walkthrough plan (for the auditor meeting):
- 7 minute intro: control mapping + high-level process.
- 12 minute live demo: Scenario 1 (role change) -> show console action -> show log emission -> open SIEM saved query -> export artifact.
- 8 minute second demo: Scenario 3 (incident) -> show alert -> ticket linkage -> postmortem snippet.
- 3 minute Q&A with prepared references (links to artifacts).

Appendices (links & quick references):
- Canonical audit log schema (draft spec link: github PR above).
- Evidence bucket policy snippet (Confluence link).
- SIEM saved queries (list and short description).
- RBAC v2 event catalog (short list included).

Notes / open questions for the team:
- Do we require signed evidence manifests for every daily SIEM export, or only for auditor-requested windows? (ops/security decision)
- How do we provide IdP assertion exports for SSO providers that limit retention? Need legal input.
- Should evaluation artifacts for models be redacted before archive to evidence bucket (PII risk)?

If you are reviewing: please add comments inline or add tasks in JIRA linked above. This is intended as the canonical demo script for the next SOC 2 readiness run.

Document history:

- 2025-02-20: added incident scenario details (Rosa)
